name: direction
title: Direction
description: DirectionProvider: sets a subtree's writing direction for both the DOM (Keyline's CSS and DOM-reading components) and Base UI (the sides tooltips, popovers and menus take; arrow keys). useDirection reads it.
whenToUse: Use it to set right-to-left or left-to-right on a subtree so layout, glyphs, popups and arrow keys all follow. It draws nothing.

parts.name: DirectionProvider
parts.description: Sets the writing direction of a subtree in both places Keyline reads it: the DOM `dir` (Keyline's CSS, logical sides, mirrored glyphs, and the components that read the DOM: toolbar, slider, scroll area, carousel) and Base UI's DirectionProvider (the side a tooltip, popover, hover card or menu takes, and arrow keys in Base UI's composite widgets). Wrap the app once, or a region whose language differs from the page. <DirectionProvider direction="rtl">…</DirectionProvider> The wrapper is `display: contents` (the `contents` class), so it adds no box. Without it every Keyline item still follows the DOM `dir`; only Base UI's positioning of `inline-start` / `inline-end` sides needs the provider.
